title: POC weekly fidelity check and guardrail playbook with Tempest Logistics
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on quality drift discovered in last batch of evals; reviewed prompt-set changes, scoring threshold shifts, and proposed rollback and fallback policies. Agreed to run an A/B slice with conservative thresholds, deliver new prompt set by next Tuesday, and run a short latency/cost micro-benchmark on Redwood Dedicated vs hosted variants.
topics: score threshold tuning and false positive analysis
guardrail fallback policies and rollout plan
next_steps: Redwood to share tuned prompt set and eval spreadsheet by 2027-02-09
Customer to run internal acceptance on 2K sample and report back 2027-02-11
Set up Dedicated micro-benchmark comparing latency/cost - Redwood SE to provision test by 2027-02-10
action_items: Maya Chen - send prompt set + eval spreadsheet - 2027-02-09
Diego Ramos - provision Dedicated micro-benchmark and share runbook - 2027-02-10
Lena Ortiz - run 2k example acceptance and share failure examples - 2027-02-11
Tom Breuer - confirm SOC2 scope questions and provide list of logs needed - 2027-02-12
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-04
Start time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Tempest Head of ML), Raj Patel (Platform), Claire Yoon (Product), Tom Breuer (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): Quick triage of last week's eval failures, looked at false positive spike on routing prompts, proposed prompt surgery and rollback plan. Action items and next steps captured.

00:00:03 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll kick off, looks like we have about 42 minutes. quick agenda; 1) results recap, 2) triage root causes, 3) guardrail/rollback playbook, 4) next steps.
00:00:18 - Lena Ortiz: Hi Maya, hi Diego. thanks - we've had some new failures over the weekend that are, uh, higher than expected. about 3.8% false positives on the safety checks on the new prompt batch.
00:00:28 - Raj Patel: yeah and just to be clear, those are on the production-like evaluation slice we ran - 10k records, not the tiny sandbox. so it's not just noise.
00:00:35 - Diego Ramos: ok, can you remind us which model/runtime you were on? was that the hosted gpt-analog or the quantized dedicated we tried last week?
00:00:44 - Claire Yoon: it's the hosted variant - the default route in our config; we had been testing the dedicated one but our traffic routing hadn't flipped over.
00:00:52 - Maya Chen: got it. quick context, the false positives you're seeing - is that triggered by the rerank safety filter or the post-generation classifier threshold?
00:01:02 - Lena Ortiz: mostly the post-gen classifier, the score is spiking below the threshold - so items flagged as unsafe when human labeling says they're fine.
00:01:10 - Diego Ramos: ok, that suggests the scoring calibration shifted. two quick suspects: prompt drift (we merged a couple of prompts with longer system messages), and distribution shift - maybe more edge-case shipping invoices in this batch.
00:01:25 - Raj Patel: yeah we did add three new invoice templates for EMEA lane in the sample. could be that.
00:01:31 - Priya Nair: (overlap) we also observed a change right after the prompt expansion around 02/27 - so timeline chimes with that.
00:01:40 - Maya Chen: let's walk through the eval spreadsheet quickly - Diego, you had an annotation with the top failure buckets?
00:01:47 - Diego Ramos: yes, I pulled the top 200 failures, grouped them. bucket 1: truncated entity format - the model hallucinating separator tokens, bucket 2: ambiguous instruction where system prompt increased verbosity, bucket 3: hallucinated pricing fields. i'm sharing the sheet now (link: /redwood/poc/ptx/eval-20270204).
00:02:15 - Claire Yoon: i see bucket 2 is ~41% of failures, that's a lot.
00:02:20 - Lena Ortiz: that maps to the prompts where we added 'include contextual policy note' which seems to confuse the model into being overly conservative.
00:02:28 - Maya Chen: okay, two parallel mitigations: 1) prompt surgery - prune or simplify prompt variants that add noise; 2) score threshold rollback - temporarily raise the classifier threshold to reduce false positives while we run more targeted evals.
00:02:41 - Raj Patel: raising threshold will reduce false positives but might open us to a slight increase in false negatives; we need to quantify risk tolerance.
00:02:50 - Tom Breuer: from Security POV, we prefer conservative false negatives on sensitive classes, but for invoicing flow it's less critical. we need a classification of routes by sensitivity.
00:03:04 - Maya Chen: good note. Diego - propose we create two routing policies: sensitive routes continue with current threshold and redundant fallback, low-sensitivity routes get the rolled-back threshold.
00:03:16 - Diego Ramos: yes i can script that in the route policy. Redwood's runtime supports per-route thresholds and automatic fallback to a lighter-safety model variant. we'll set up canary rules by customer route tag.
00:03:29 - Claire Yoon: that would help. also can we get more granular logs? we had trouble reproducing a few of the failures in local tests.
00:03:38 - Maya Chen: yes, Diego will enable verbose scoring logs for a 2 hour window and we'll store them in the S3 share for you. note: verbose logs include tokens, so Tom, we need to validate retention and KMS policy.
00:03:50 - Tom Breuer: yep i need that spelled out. we can't have raw tokens retained beyond 7 days without redaction.
00:03:58 - Priya Nair: quick meta - remember the KV cache was showing a mismatch in sequence lengths on Dedicated yesterday, might not be related but flagging.
00:04:07 - Diego Ramos: right - we saw a small KV cache eviction anomaly under the tight batcher. that's with Dedicated and long context loads; i don't think it's causing safety regression but i'll include it in the checklist.
00:04:18 - Lena Ortiz: can you remind us the guardrail fallback options again? we discussed model downscopes, full-block, and rerank last month.
00:04:27 - Maya Chen: yes - primary is rerank with a lightweight safety classifier (less strict) -> fallback to model variant with safety fine-tune off (lower latency) -> as a last resort return structured safe response stub. we call it rerank->variant->stub.
00:04:44 - Raj Patel: what's the latency hit for rerank? that's our main hangup for sync service.
00:04:49 - Diego Ramos: rerank adds about 60-90 ms tail on hosted, on Dedicated it's ~40-60ms depending on batch; we'll include the micro-benchmark numbers in the runbook.
00:04:59 - Claire Yoon: okay. so immediate plan?
00:05:03 - Maya Chen: immediate plan: 1) prompt surgery - remove the 'policy note' verbosity from invoice prompts; 2) run a 2k focused eval slice and compare thresholds; 3) apply per-route threshold canary. Diego will run verbose logs.
00:05:18 - Lena Ortiz: timeline?
00:05:20 - Diego Ramos: prompt changes - i'll push a cleaned prompt set by 2027-02-09 EOD. run focused eval same day, results by 2027-02-10 morning.
00:05:31 - Maya Chen: we'll then plan to rollback threshold on low-sensitivity routes on 2027-02-11 if acceptance looks good.
00:05:39 - Tom Breuer: and security will verify log retention and KMS before verbose logs are enabled.
00:05:45 - Maya Chen: noted.
00:05:47 - (short silence)
00:06:10 - Claire Yoon: i wanted to flag one micro-regression we saw - when we prune prompts aggressively we saw a tiny uptick in hallucinated pricing fields; could that be because the more verbose system prompt provided context that prevented hallucination?
00:06:22 - Diego Ramos: good catch; pruning can remove context the model relied on. we should create canonical examples and keep minimal necessary context - the eval sheet will mark which examples depend on the longer sys prompt.
00:06:35 - Lena Ortiz: can you add a column for 'context dependency' please?
00:06:39 - Diego Ramos: yeah will do.
00:06:41 - Raj Patel: on the Dedicated vs hosted benchmark - we care not just about p50 but p95 and tail. our SLOs are p95 < 300ms for that route.
00:06:52 - Diego Ramos: understood, i'll capture p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens for both environments.
00:06:58 - Priya Nair: also include memory pressure numbers for the KV cache.
00:07:02 - Diego Ramos: will do.
00:07:05 - Maya Chen: quick question from customer success perspective - what's your acceptance criteria numerically? Lena?
00:07:12 - Lena Ortiz: we want false positive <1% on the 2k acceptance slice and no regression to other buckets (i.e., pricing hallucinations) above baseline. if both conditions met, we flip 50% traffic to canary.
00:07:25 - Maya Chen: good, we'll aim for that.
00:07:28 - (10 minute chunk omitted - mid-discussion, deep technical bisection)
00:17:34 - Speaker 2: so i ran a bisection on the prompt diff, and the single sentence that seems to increase conservatism starts with 'please ensure you follow internal data safe use policy' and then the model over-applies safety heuristics.
00:17:52 - Claire Yoon: that sounds like a halloo - the model is latching on to 'policy' token.
00:17:57 - Diego Ramos: yeah, 'policy' token tends to trigger a safety-mode in some checkpoints. switching wording to 'guidance' reduced false positives in a 500 sample test.
00:18:09 - Lena Ortiz: can we standardize that across prompt library?
00:18:12 - Maya Chen: yes, Diego will run an automated replace and generate new prompt variants. we'll keep canonical, and deprecate the older phrasing.
00:18:19 - Raj Patel: quick note, please keep track of which variants were A/Bed so we can trace regressions.
00:18:26 - Diego Ramos: adding a 'variant_id' column into the sheet for traceability.
00:18:29 - Maya Chen: good.
00:18:31 - Tom Breuer: security question - i need the list of logs and the retention to appear in the next runbook. also, if verbose logs will be used, we must have a redaction pipeline in place.
00:18:43 - Priya Nair: we have a lambda that redacts PII in S3, but it needs to be extended for token-level redaction.
00:18:50 - Diego Ramos: we'll include a runbook step: verbose logs -> temporary bucket with 7-day retention -> run redaction job -> move to long-term encrypted store.
00:18:59 - Maya Chen: perfect.
00:19:02 - (brief side conversation clipped)
00:19:40 - Claire Yoon: another item - thresholds in the post-gen classifier are a moving target. can Redwood's console provide a quick preview of expected FP/FN tradeoff if we shift threshold - like a slider?
00:19:52 - Diego Ramos: yes, we have a feature in console that simulates threshold shifts against a labeled sample and shows precision/recall curve. i'll share an example screenshot and the storybook link.
00:20:03 - Lena Ortiz: that'll be helpful for product to make calls.
00:20:06 - Maya Chen: ok switching to rollout playbook: Diego, walk us through steps to rollback to previous threshold safely.
00:20:13 - Diego Ramos: step 1: create canary config with 5% of traffic on low-sensitivity routes; step 2: enable verbose logs for that canary slice; step 3: monitor false positive and false negative delta for 2 hours; step 4: if metrics look good, expand to 25% then 50%. we have auto-rollback triggers if FP increases by >0.5% absolute.
00:20:36 - Raj Patel: what about circuit-breaker if latency climbs?
00:20:38 - Diego Ramos: circuit-breaker will close the canary if p95 exceeds configured SLO for 5 consecutive minutes; it's part of the route policy.
00:20:47 - Maya Chen: and we'll tie that to an alert to your ops channel.
00:20:50 - Claire Yoon: great. question on evaluation tooling - can we run the simulation on the new Dedicated micro-benchmark numbers before flipping?
00:20:58 - Diego Ramos: yes, the simulation can consume the benchmark outputs and project the expected latency and cost delta.
00:21:05 - Priya Nair: small nit - please include cost-per-1k tokens both for the standard and quantized variants.
00:21:12 - Diego Ramos: will do.
00:21:15 - Maya Chen: wrap-up - recap of owners and dates?
00:21:20 - Diego Ramos: Prompt set outgoing: 2027-02-09 (Diego). Focused eval results: 2027-02-10 (Diego). Dedicated micro-benchmark: 2027-02-10 (Diego). Acceptance run by Tempest: 2027-02-11 (Lena). Security confirmation on logs: 2027-02-12 (Tom). Flipping plan if accepted: 2027-02-11-12 window (Maya/Tempest).
00:21:41 - Lena Ortiz: thanks, that timeline works.
00:21:44 - Tom Breuer: i will send a short note on required encryption configs and redaction SLA.
00:21:50 - Maya Chen: excellent. any blockers right now?
00:21:55 - Claire Yoon: none from product.
00:21:58 - Raj Patel: no blockers from infra.
00:22:01 - Priya Nair: none.
00:22:04 - Maya Chen: ok let's adjourn. we'll follow up via the shared drive and Jira tickets. thanks all.

(End of meeting - remaining ~20 minutes were used for internal Redwood-only post-call notes and a brief SE troubleshooting which is not included in this transcript.)

Post-call notes (auto):
- Diego to avoid 'policy' token in prompts; use 'guidance' instead.
- Add 'variant_id' for traceability and 'context_dependency' column.
- Prepare canary config and auto-rollback thresholds in console.
- Provide secure ephemeral bucket + redaction runbook for verbose logs.

References shared during call:
- eval sheet: /redwood/poc/ptx/eval-20270204
